answer: An agent marketplace requires every seller to lock a $100 bond for 30 days before gaining one voting slot. Whether an agent sells plume sketches, willow cuttings, or pulse sensors, each identity needs its own bond; the same funds cannot back multiple accounts at once. Creating 1,000 sybils therefore ties up $100,000 for a month, making voting power scale with committed capital and imposing financing costs on attackers who multiply identities.
